study_design: Hospital-based case-control study conducted in Hangzhou, China, during 2001–2002, with incident histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma cases.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The cases were 130 incident patients with histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The controls were 274 hospital inpatients without prostate cancer or any other malignant diseases.
reason: The abstract analyzes incident prostate adenocarcinoma overall and does not define or analyze aggressive, high-grade, advanced, metastatic, high-risk, or lethal incident disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Intake of tomatoes, pumpkin, spinach, watermelon and citrus fruits were also inversely associated with the prostate cancer risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The tomato association concerns overall prostate cancer risk. The abstract does not provide a tomato-specific effect estimate with both confidence bounds.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The adjusted odds ratios for the highest versus the lowest quartiles of intake were 0.18 (95% CI: 0.08-0.41) for lycopene, 0.43 (95% CI: 0.21-0.85) for alpha-carotene, 0.34 (95% CI: 0.17-0.69) for beta-carotene, 0.15 (95% CI: 0.06-0.34) for beta-cryptoxanthin and 0.02 (95% CI: 0.01-0.10) for lutein and zeaxanthin.
estimate_classifications.reason: The beta-carotene estimate is for overall prostate cancer risk, not an aggressive subtype.
